Certified type:
- Category: This is a "weighing module" — under R76, modules are indicators or weighing modules. The category field examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter". A "weighing module" is likely an indicator/complete weighing module. I'll use "Weighing module" as the category.
- type_designations: ["QBase"]
- module_designation: "Weighing module" — hmm, module_designation options are "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Actually for R76 modules, the module could be "Weight indicator" or similar. The certificate says "A weighing module, Type: QBase". I'll set module_designation to "Weighing module" — the schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null, but those are examples for R60. I think the best fit is "Weighing module". Actually the schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null — but these are for load cell certificates. For R76 module certs, module designation could be like "Weighing module". Hmm. The schema seems restrictive but I think it's fine to put "Weighing module" since it's a weighing module per R76-1. Alternatively null. I'll go with "Weighing module".

Recommendation:
- id: "R76" (canonical, e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60"). The recommendation is R 76-1. Canonical: "R76". Edition: 2006? The schema says edition (int). "R 76-1:2006" — edition 2006. Amendment: null.

- accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]

The schema doesn't have revision for test reports, but revision_history covers cert revisions. I could include revision in id or add a field. Better keep to schema: id "NMi-2477454-01 revision 1"? Hmm, rule 8 says don't fabricate. I'll include the revision info in the id string since the schema doesn't have a revision field... Actually, adding extra fields isn't prohibited explicitly but sticking to schema is safer. I'll do id: "NMi-2477454-01" and role type_evaluation_report. Hmm but revision 1 matters. Characteristics:

The table on page 2:
- Accuracy class: (III) or (IIII)
- Maximum capacity: Max ≤ 30 kg → maximum_capacity: value {min: null, max: 30}, unit "kg"
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 1 g → verification_scale_interval: {min: 1, max: null}, unit "g"
- Weighing range(s): Single interval, Multi-interval → weighing_ranges: ["single interval", "multi-interval"] or two booleans. I'll do a type_level characteristic weighing_ranges with value ["single interval", "multi-interval"]? Value must be number | {min,max} | string. A list isn't allowed. Hmm. I could make two characteristics: weighing_range_single_interval: value "single interval"... Better: "weighing_ranges": value string "single interval or multi-interval"? Or config_level. Actually "Single interval / Multi-interval" — the module supports both single-interval and multi-interval instruments. I could represent as config_level axis "weighing range type": conditions "single interval" and "multi-interval" with respective n values. The table then gives max number of scale intervals per range type:
  - one weighing range: n ≤ 6000
  - multi-interval: n ≤ 3000 per partial weighing range
  
  That's actually a config axis! "Maximum number of scale intervals" varies by configuration: single-interval → 6000; multi-interval → 3000 per partial weighing range.

So config_level:
- attribute: max_number_of_scale_intervals, axis: "weighing range configuration"
  - condition "single interval (one weighing range)": value {min: null, max: 6000}, unit null (dimensionless count)
  - condition "multi-interval (per partial weighing range)": value {min: null, max: 3000}

- maximum_number_of_partial_weighing_ranges: 2
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- Power supply voltage: two variants:
  - variant without CPU board: 4.4 – 5.25 V DC (through USB)
  - variant with CPU board: 12 V DC
  
  This is config_level (axis: power supply variant / CPU board variant):
  - condition "variant without CPU board (through USB)": value {min: 4.4, max: 5.25}, unit "V", DC
  - condition "variant with CPU board": value 12, unit "V"

- Software identification table:
  - A/D Board software identification: version numbers 010 (ID 6153), 011 (ID 5232), 030 (ID 1446)
  - CPU software identification (QBase C2): version 001, ID 8324

Actually the schema says model_family include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The power supply variants could be seen as config axis. I'll use config_level only, and skip model_family.
